items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: They were older guys, and they knew all these people. They would say, 'That's Ben Webster' and 'That's Chu Berry' and 'That's Roy Eldridge.' ... Roy Eldridge used to come to Washington here. When he was in town, Sammy would have his guitar... and he would go around and see Roy.

ctx.x: John Malachi (5/7/83), Part 3, with Bryant DuPre:

After leaving Illinois, I came back to Washington, and then I took a gig in a club -- I was sort of a supper club type place -- with a bandleader. His name was Al Dunn. He had a title that everybody used to call him -- "Al, it's got to be done." Anyway, he had this quartet that had Frank Wess on tenor saxophone, and William Eldridge, a bassist, Roy Eldridge's cousin, on bass, and of course Al Dunn on drums. During that time this club featured major artists. It would bring in singers and sometimes even big bands.

While I was there, Billie Holiday came in. I think she was in there for two weeks, and we worked with her. After Billie Holiday left, I was with... I stayed there about two months, I guess, and I got a call from Dinah Washington. I went on a job with her, I guess, for about at least four or five weeks. I don't remember where we played. It seems like to me that we played some theatres or something.
